rv: While this isn't the most technically impressive noir, it has some of the most iconic and quintessential scenes in the genre. If you haven't figured it out yet, this is a MUST WATCH noir! So sit back, relax, and get ready to start practicing your Tommy Udo laugh.

This is an often underrated film noir that cleverly uses a noir concept in reverse, Normal concept is good person does a bad thing and gets in trouble with the law. Here a bad guy does a good thing and gets in trouble with the bad guys. I believe Richard Widmark was nominated for Best Supporting Actor for this role. Victor Mature, normally a pedestrian actor, does well here. The supporting cast is excellent beyond Widmark - Taylor Holmes, Brian Donlevy and Karl Malden in a smaller role.

Veteran cowboy star Bob Steele played a fictionalized Billy the Kid in six low budget westerns for Producers Releasing Corporation in the 1940-41 season. The real life William Bonney had been a homocidal outlaw-gunfighter who was killed at age 21. His cinema adventures had previously been whitewashed to be played by Johnny Mack Brown, Roy Rogers and Robert Taylor. Steele's youthful athletic hero image made him perfect for the part, but he left the series to join the western trio of the Three Mesquiteers at Republic in 1941.
